carbendazim (field recommendation) in combination with abamectin at their respective (LC50) values resulted in maximum synergism against A. flavus spores.
the chemical compatibility of the avermectins with common fungicides is not consistent and depends upon the type of fungicide and the concentration of the test insecticides.
carbendazim and mancozeb were found to have the most antagonistic effects with the avermectins, while lufenuron and emamectin were found to be synergistic with carbendazim.

chemical compatibility of averectins and chitinsynthesis inhibitors with common fungicide against A. flavus.
the chemical compatibility of insecticides with common fungicides and the effect of these combinations on A. flavus.

the chemical compatibility of abamectin and emamectin-benzoate with the chitin synthesis inhibitors, novaluron, lufenuron and carbendazim with the benzimidazole fungicides, carbendazin and chlorothalonil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combinations of fungicides and insecticides were antagonistic at lower concentrations and synergistic at higher concentrations.
carbendazim and mancozeb at their field recommended concentration are antagonistic to abamectin and novaluron and antagonistic and synergistic to lufenuron and emamectin respectively.
the combinations of abamectin with chlorothalonil, mancozeb and carbendazim were antagonistic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combinations of carbendazim (at LC50 value) and abamectin (at LC50 and field recommended concentrations) were the most effective in controlling the spore germination in A. flavus.

, the combination of carbendazim with abamectins and lufenuron is not recommended as it may result in antagonism.
